arxiv-2103-14586.title: Understanding Robustness of Transformers for Image Classification
arxiv-2103-14586.creator: Srinadh Bhojanapalli ∗, Ayan Chakrabarti ∗, Daniel Glasner ∗, Daliang Li ∗, Thomas Unterthiner ∗, Andreas Veit ∗
arxiv-2103-14586.description: Abstract Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have long been the architecture of choice for computer vision tasks. Recently, Transformer-based architectures like Vision Transformer (ViT) have matched or even surpassed ResNets for image classification. However, details of the Transformer architecture –such as the use of non-overlapping patches– lead one to wonder whether these networks are as robust.

arxiv-2106-07129.title: A Path-Counting Analysis of Phase Shifts in Box-Ball Systems
arxiv-2106-07129.creator: Nicholas M. ERCOLANI and Jonathan RAMALHEIRA-TSU
arxiv-2106-07129.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Nicholas M. ERCOLANI and Jonathan RAMALHEIRA-TSU. In this paper, we perform a detailed analysis of the phase shift phenomenon of the classical soliton cellular automaton known as the box-ball system, ultimately resulting in a statement and proof of a formula describing this phase shift. This phenomenon has been observed since the nineties, when the system was first introduced by Takahashi and Satsuma, but no explicit global description was made beyond its observation.

arxiv-2306-09161.title: A kinetic study of black hole activation by local plasma injection into the inner magnetosphere 2023 A kinetic study of black hole activation by local plasma injection into the inner magnetosphere –
arxiv-2306-09161.creator: Idan Niv, Omer Bromberg, Amir Levinson, Benoit Cerutti, Benjamin Crinquand
arxiv-2306-09161.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Idan Niv, Omer Bromberg, Amir Levinson, Benoit Cerutti, Benjamin Crinquand. An issue of considerable interest in the theory of jet formation by the Blandford-Znajek mechanism, is how plasma is being continuously supplied to the magnetosphere to maintain it in a force-free state. Injection of electron-positron pairs via annihilation of MeV photons, emitted from a hot accretion flow, has been shown to be a viable possibility, but requires a high enough accretion rate.

arxiv-2402-06318.title: TimEHR: Image-based Time Series Generation for Electronic Health Records
arxiv-2402-06318.creator: Hojjat Karami, Mary-Anne Hartley, David Atienza, Anisoara Ionescu
arxiv-2402-06318.description: Abstract Time series in Electronic Health Records (EHRs) present unique challenges for generative models, such as irregular sampling, missing values, and high dimensionality. In this paper, we propose a novel generative adversarial network (GAN) model, TimEHR , to generate time series data from EHRs. In particular, TimEHR treats time series as images and is based on two conditional GANs.

arxiv-2412-07181.title: Modeling and Simulating Rydberg Atom Quantum Computers for Hardware-Software Co-design with PachinQo
arxiv-2412-07181.creator: Jason Zev Ludmir, Yuqian Huo, Nicholas S. DiBrita, Tirthak Patel
arxiv-2412-07181.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jason Zev Ludmir, Yuqian Huo, Nicholas S. DiBrita, Tirthak Patel. Quantum computing has the potential to accelerate various domains: scientific computation, machine learning, and optimization. Recently, Rydberg atom quantum computing has emerged as a promising quantum computing technology, especially with the demonstration of the zonal addressing architecture. However, this demonstration is only compatible with one type of quantum algorithm, and extending it to compile and execute general quantum algorithms is a challenge.

arxiv-2503-14959.creator: Justin Iurman, Emilien Wansart, Maxime Goffart, Benoit Donnet
arxiv-2503-14959.description: Abstract Lightweight Tunnels ( Lwt s) in the Linux kernel enable efficient per-route tunneling and are widely used by protocols such as I n Situ O perations, A dministration, and M aintenance ( Ioam ), S egment R outing over Ipv6 ( Sr v6), and R outing P rotocol for L ow-Power and Lossy Networks ( Rpl ).

arxiv-2505-16454.title: Parallel Phase-shifting Digital Ghost Holography
arxiv-2505-16454.creator: Shuhei Yoshida
arxiv-2505-16454.description: Abstract The ghost imaging (GI) technique, which has attracted attention as a highly sensitive and noise-resistant technique, employs a spatially modulated illuminating light and a single-pixel detector. Generally, the information acquired by GI is the transmittance or reflectance distribution of an object. A method has also been proposed to measure the complex amplitude by applying digital holography (DH) techniques.

pmc-11505647.title: Retinopathy of Prematurity in Eight Portuguese Neonatal Intensive Care Units: Incidence, Risk Factors, and Progression—A Prospective Multicenter Study
pmc-11505647.creator: Mariza Fevereiro-Martins, Ana Carolina Santos, Carlos Marques-Neves, Manuel Bicho, Hercília Guimarães, on behalf of the GenE-ROP Study Group, Ru-Jeng Teng
pmc-11505647.description: Background/Objectives: Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is a retinal neovascular disease affecting preterm infants. Identifying risk factors for its development and progression is critical for effective screening and prevention. This study aimed to analyze the incidence of ROP and identify key risk factors for its development and progression.

pmc-11656206.title: Validation of a Simple HPLC/UV Method for Assay and In Vitro Release of Glycosaminoglycan from Pharmaceutical Formulations
pmc-11656206.creator: Gokselin Ozgen, Nahide Zeren Arda Ozturk, Gokce Turan, Merve Turk, Evren Homan Gokce, Ozgen Ozer, Hayriye Icin, Gonul Kayar, Enis Isik, Udaya Kumar Dude, Sakine Tuncay Tanrıverdi
pmc-11656206.description: This study encompasses the validation of a simple, rapid, and sensitive HPLC/UV method developed in accordance with the guidelines set by ICH Q2(R2) for obtaining the active pharmaceutical ingredient from the glycosaminoglycan family in topical formulations. Previous methods reported for analyzing glycosaminoglycans in semisolid formulations are relatively complex and time-consuming, involving extraction, purification, and derivatization.

pmc-11678956.title: Measurement Properties of Wearable Kinematic-Based Data Collection Systems to Evaluate Ball Kicking in Soccer: A Systematic Review with Evidence Gap Map †
pmc-11678956.creator: Luiz H. Palucci Vieira, Filipe M. Clemente, Rui M. Silva, Kelly R. Vargas-Villafuerte, Felipe P. Carpes
pmc-11678956.description: Kinematic assessment of ball kicking may require significant human effort (e.g., traditional vision-based tracking systems). Wearables offer a potential solution to reduce processing time. This systematic review collated measurement properties (validity, reliability, and/or accuracy) of wearable kinematic-based technology systems used to evaluate soccer kicking. Seven databases were searched for studies published on or before April 2024.

pmc-13259748.creator: Wei Zhou, Lizhen Wang, Mengxing Li, Xuan Liu, Qing Fang, Yang Yu, Songjie Zhang, Jing Guo, Rui Chang, Cheng Zhang, Tongliang Zhou, Yang Liu, Xiaoxia Ren, Honglin Liu, Lihong Liu
